title: S117 11.3 Client Handling of Unsolicited Responses Not Suitable for the

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Many server responses and response codes are only meaningful in authenticated or even selected state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Many server responses and response codes are only meaningful in authenticated or even selected state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Before authentication, clients SHOULD ignore any responses other than CAPABILITY and server status responses (Section 7.1), as well as any response codes other than CAPABILITY.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD ignore the ALERT response code until after TLS (whether using STARTTLS or TLS negotiation on an Implicit TLS port) or a SASL security layer with confidentiality protection has been successfully negotiated.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Unless explicitly allowed by an IMAP extension, when not in selected state, clients MUST ignore responses / response codes related to message and mailbox status such as FLAGS, EXIST, EXPUNGE, and FETCH.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Nothing prevents a server (or an on-path attacker) from sending such invalid responses in cleartext before STARTTLS/AUTHENTICATE commands are issued. Before authentication, clients SHOULD ignore any responses other than CAPABILITY and server status responses.
actions: expand set of processable server responses
